extractedText: AI Chatbots Are Quietly Causing A New Relationship Problem — And More Couples Are Struggling With ItFleurine TidemanUpdated Fri, July 31, 2026 at 5:18 PM UTC0Entering a monogamous relationship comes with a long list of conversations about boundaries. What counts as crossing a line? Is flirting with someone else harmless or hurtful? Should you tell your partner if someone asks you out? How do you navigate friendships with exes? Is watching **** or subscribing to ******** acceptable within the relationship?There’s no universal answer. Every couple gets to decide what commitment, intimacy and trust look like for them.Also Read: I Went On A Date With An AI Chatbot. It Felt So Real — Until He Revealed His Strange Fixation.But couples today are facing a new question that wasn’t part of the conversation for most relationships formed before the rise of artificial intelligence: Where do AI companions fit into the boundaries of a romantic relationship?AI companion apps, such as Joi AI, eva AI and Candy.ai, allow users to create digital partners they can chat with, confide in and build ongoing emotional connections with. While some people use them for entertainment, companionship or emotional support, others are forming relationships that can feel surprisingly intimate. Naturally this raises a complicated new question: Can an emotional connection with an AI bot be a form of infidelity?For some couples, the answer has become personal. HuffPost spoke to people who discovered their partners were engaging with AI chatbots in ways they felt crossed a relationship boundary, as well as experts exploring how we should understand these new forms of connection. Note: Some names have been shortened or changed to protect privacy.‘It felt like AI was stroking his ego.’“My boyfriend and I were watching a movie, and then he went to take a phone call,” Olivia, 31, told HuffPost. “I clicked on his ChatGPT tab and found he had been using it extensively. It wasn’t just questions about our relationship or complaints about me, it got so personal. It felt like the AI was stroking his ego, and he was confiding emotional things to it that he hadn’t told me. We got into a huge argument about it.”Relationship: These Are The Worst Foods To Eat Before Oral ***Anna, 42, had a similar experience after noticing a charge on the couple’s credit card that turned out to be for an AI dating companion.“I asked my husband about it, and he didn’t see anything wrong with it. He even showed me the app,” she said. “I felt really weird about his ‘girlfriend’ on there and their chats, but he said it was all fake, so why would it matter? We haven’t talked about it again, but it keeps bothering me.”For others, the idea of using AI romantically was enough to change how they viewed a potential partner.“Last summer, I was dating a guy, and he told me that he used an AI dating companion to practice flirting,” said Kelly, 22. “It was an ick, and I didn’t continue things.” It wasn’t just questions about our relationship or complaints about me, it got so personal. It felt like the AI was stroking his ego, and he was confiding emotional things to it that he hadn’t told me.OliviaThese experiences are becoming increasingly common as AI continues to creep into more personal areas of our lives. It’s not just handling our grocery list anymore. According to LELO’s 2026 Futurist Report, 60% of people aged 18 to 45 have used AI in their intimate lives in some way, whether to plan a date, navigate an argument, draft a message or explore intimacy. Yep, we’re all firmly in a tech ********* at this point.Health: 'AI Psychosis' Is A Real Problem — Here's Who's Most VulnerableWhy might someone use an AI chatbot while in a relationship?Jaime Bronstein is a licensed clinical social worker and the resident relationship expert at Joi AI, an app that offers users AI companions ranging from virtual girlfriends to chatbot versions inspired by celebrities. The company bills itself as “the enemy of dating apps,” positioning AI companionship as an alternative to traditional dating.Bronstein feels the appeal isn’t always about replacing a partner, but rather filling the inevitable gaps that exist in any relationship.“With an AI companion, there’s a better sense of freedom to think out loud, vent about a bad day or rehearse a hard conversation before you have it for real, without dumping everything on a human partner who has limits,” Bronstein told HuffPost. “It can help people whose partners work late at night or live far away and aren’t as available to chat. It can be helpful to bridge the gap that our human relationships inevitably create.”At a time when loneliness remains widespread, it’s easy to see why some people find comfort in an always-available companion that never gets tired, distracted or busy.Like this article?
